learning_outcomes.text: Master the algebra of complex numbers; know how to deal with exponential and trigonometric functions and their inverses.
Explicitly solve initial value problems, in particular using the Laplace transform.
Represent periodic functions in Fourier series.
Determine the Laplace and Fourier transformations of simple functions.
Know and apply some basic properties of Laplace and Fourier transforms.
Use Fourier analysis methods and properties in the context of signal processing, image processing and data compression.
Identify holomorphic functions using Cauchy-Riemann conditions. Calculate integrals of functions in the complex plane.
Represent functions of complex variables in power series and identify singularities.
Calculate integrals using the residue theorem.
Implement computational applications of Fourier analysis and complex analysis using MATLAB.

syllabus_topics: Complex numbers. Euler's formula, polar representation and roots.
Second order linear equations with constant coefficients. Applications: RLC circuits; forced oscillations and resonance.
Laplace transform and its properties. Application to solving initial value problems.
Application of the convolution theorem to time-invariant linear systems. Filters.
Computational applications of Fourier analysis using MATLAB.
Complex variable functions. Analytical functions. Cauchy-Riemann conditions.
Integrals of complex functions in the complex plane. Cauchy's theorem.
Taylor and Laurent series. Singularities and poles.
Residue theorem. Applications: calculation of integrals.

assessment_methods.method: Final written test (on the subject not assessed in the first test)

assessment_rules: For assessment throughout the semester, the minimum grade in any of the written tests is 8.0, and the weighted average of the two tests and the work has a minimum grade of 9.5. For assessment by exam, the exam is in person and has a minimum score of 9.5 points. Students may have to undertake an oral examination whenever the instructor deems it necessary.
